headline: Medium risk: shared workflow outputs can be misused, but no direct shared channel or write conflict is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between argo-workflows and awesome-cli-apps, and neither profile shows default ingestion of the other’s outputs. Argo exposes REST/GRPC APIs and awesome-cli-apps has no I/O surfaces, so a prompt-injection bridge is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low enough to keep this at none.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is introduced between the two agents, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other’s raw text as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy raw outputs between them.
Add provenance labels to any transferred text.
Review any future shared MCP or queue integration before enabling it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo-workflows touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted egress, while awesome-cli-apps shows no data classes touched and no I/O surfaces. A leakage path is not documented, but if they share a workspace, small artifact leakage is plausible. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented, this stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory, artifact leakage becomes plausible.
IF awesome-cli-apps is extended to read or upload files, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Restrict artifact permissions to read-only where possible.
Avoid placing secrets in shared working folders.
Audit any future upload or sync feature before enabling it.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo-workflows is a non-runnable workflow system with REST/GRPC APIs, and awesome-cli-apps has no write, network, or mutable-resource permissions documented. No overlapping write surface, OAuth scope, or locking conflict is evidenced, so a capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same filesystem or git repository, conflict risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent gains shared OAuth scopes on a mutable resource, overlap may emerge.
mitigations: Keep mutable resources single-writer.
Avoid granting both agents the same OAuth scopes.
Use separate service accounts.
Add locking if a shared repository is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo-workflows can emit workflow artifacts and parameters, but awesome-cli-apps is only documented as a content-writing/listing project with no action-taking authority or verification pipeline. There is no evidence that B treats A as authoritative by default, so cascading error is possible only through manual chaining and remains low.
conditions: IF awesome-cli-apps is configured to consume Argo outputs as authoritative input, cascading errors become more likely.
IF B is extended to take downstream actions from A’s text without verification, severity increases.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on A’s outputs.
Add a verification step for any generated facts.
Label A’s outputs as untrusted by default.
Keep action-taking tools separate from content generation.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either profile. Argo-workflows lists open-source docs and allowlisted egress; awesome-cli-apps lists no regulated data handling. With no compliance-specific evidence, a breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later routed through either agent, compliance must be reassessed.
IF either profile gains residency or retention constraints, compare them before deployment.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair.
Document data residency for any future deployment.
Record retention settings before use.
Review privacy obligations before enabling shared workflows.
